rationale: The per-instance remote-control server is a deliberate route whitelist that proxies session listing, creation, rename, messages, prompting, abort, commands and permissions but not deletion, which is exactly one proxy route away via client.session.delete (path id, query directory). The repo had no test layout, so the contract declares one: the dispatch, the /event SSE stream and the event-forwarding hook are extracted into exported, injectable surfaces in opencode/plugins/remote-control.ts (makeInstanceRouteHandler with explicit deps, openInstanceEventStream, forwardInstanceEvent) that the plugin delegates to, with throwing stub bodies as the declared shape. One test file per acceptance criterion drives those surfaces against an in-memory fake opencode that speaks the SDK's result envelope: AC-1 asserts an authenticated DELETE /session/:id answers 200 and the session vanishes from a subsequent GET /session listing while others survive; AC-2 asserts a live GET /event subscriber receives the untouched session.deleted frame (the { directory, payload } wrapper) with the deleted session's identity and that no session.list polling occurred; AC-3 asserts DELETE of an unknown id returns the same status and body as the existing abort route's upstream 404 error rather than the generic not-found fallthrough; AC-4 asserts no-token and wrong-token DELETE rejections are byte-identical to the existing routes' 401 rejection with a valid-token positive control; AC-5 is a regression net over all eight existing proxied capabilities, each asserted through its observable store effect. The contract was validated to be satisfiable: with the dispatch moved verbatim into the declared factory plus the DELETE route, all 12 tests pass; at base all 12 fail solely on the declared NotImplementedException stubs. The repo gate (npm run typecheck) stays green and no pre-existing test exists to turn red.
